title: Wage Labour and Capital
author: Karl Marx
subject: Political Economy
context: Based on lectures Marx delivered in 1847 to the German Workingmen's Club in Brussels, this work provides a straightforward and accessible explanation of the economic relationships under capitalism, particularly how labor becomes a commodity and how wages are determined.
relatesToToday: Directly applies to inflation and paycheck anxiety. As productivity jumps due to AI and automation, real purchasing power drops while rent and groceries become more expensive. It explains why a salary raise of 3% feels like a pay cut when living costs jump by 7%.
keyTakeaways: Wages are the price of a specific commodity: human labor-power.
Capitalists buy labor-power to generate surplus value (profit) by selling the products of that labor for more than the wages paid.
The interests of wage labor and capital are diametrically opposed; as capital grows, the worker becomes relatively poorer and more dependent.
